description: I'm a BCA student and developer interested in AI, web development, UI/UX, graphic design, and space exploration. I enjoy turning ideas into creative, interactive digital experiences. Our goal is to build an immersive Moon and Mars exploration archive that brings forgotten NASA equipment and its stories to life. Looking for passionate teammates skilled in astronomy, space research, 3D design, animation, data visualization, and storytelling. Let's build something impactful!
summary:
Relic Finder is an innovative 3D museum of space history, which revives NASA’s outdated and already retired space vehicles, and was created as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 competition. 

The application allows a user to walk around the virtual museum, take pictures of the various space relics, project the pictures on different surfaces, and enter the exhibition rooms to learn about the history, construction, scientific contribution, and location of the machines. In addition, every exhibit has a mini-game, which reveals its important aspects of the earlier given technologies.

The application consists of ten famous relics including Apollo Lunar Module, NEAR Shoemaker, Kepler, Viking, Ingenuity, Voyager 1, etc. 

The main purpose of our application is to help forgotten machines be transformed into educational experience full of curiosity regarding science achievements, engineering, and human history of space exploration.
details:
What does Relic Finder do?

The Relic Finder provides an exciting opportunity to explore NASA's old space hardware because it is a 3D interactive museum. This museum provides users with access to the history of space exploration hardware left on Moon, Mars, or asteroids.

The users of the museum have the chance to interact with the functioning of exact replicas of this hardware and know the story of each of the machines.

How does it work?

There are six stages in the experience:

  • Explore: Walk around a first-person 3D museum and learn about different spacecrafts and items from space.
  • Capture: Use a camera that can take pictures of artifacts.
  • Project: Attach the object being photographed to the surface of the wall or floor.
  • Discover: Go through the photograph and enter the exhibition dedicated to that object.
  • Learn and Operate: Gather knowledge from historical perspectives, technical details, and other important contributions about space objects.
  • Finalize: Explore all ten exhibitions of the museum.

In addition, users can go back to any action or the main museum.

What does it cover?

The project features ten space relics:

  • Apollo Lunar Module
  • NEAR Shoemaker
  • Kepler Space Telescope
  • Viking Lander
  • Spirit and Opportunity
  • Ingenuity Helicopter
  • Hubble Space Telescope
  • Voyager 1
  • Cassini-Huygens
  • Pioneer 10

The exhibits are diverse and feature different topics from space exploration, like lunar landings, asteroid exploration, planetary science, space telescopes, as well as interstellar exploration. 

Benefits and Intended Impact

Relic Finder simplifies space science for people in the younger age group. It provides an innovative way of education by presenting information in an engaging form. 

  • Expected results of the initiative are: 
  • - Promoting awareness of retired NASA exploration tools, their status, and fate.
  • - Making learning about space exploration history interesting through storytelling.
  • - Teaching about spacecraft engineering.
  • - Demonstrating contributions of certain devices to science.
  • - Providing education in engineering at a basic level.

Technology and Tools Used

  • HTML5 – Application structure and content.
  • CSS3 – Interface design, layouts, animations, and responsive styling.
  • JavaScript – Interactive functionality, navigation, controls, and mission logic.
  • Three.js (r128) – Real-time 3D rendering and immersive museum environments.
  • GLTFLoader – Loading and displaying 3D spacecraft models.
  • GLB – Embedded 3D models and associated assets.
  • Google Fonts – Typography using Unbounded and Inter.
  • Cloudflare Pages – Public website hosting and deployment.

The project uses embedded models, textures, and mission information, avoiding the need for a database, backend server, or API keys.

Creativity and Innovation

The main idea of the project is to create an interactive virtual museum from a traditional education site. The photo-and-projection mechanism enables a new form of connection between the main museum site and separate exhibitions by changing the format of navigation from browsing regular sites to moving in a 3D environment and becoming a part of the stories of the particular spacecraft.

Factors Considered

The emphasis of the development process was placed on accessibility, educational value, immersion, effectiveness, as well as simplicity.

The application works directly in the modern browser without needing installation, registration, dedicated server, and payment for API usage.

The project is an independent educational project rather than an official NASA product.
